newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swissair first half '97 looks good-COO.
newsitem.headline: Swissair first half '97 looks good-COO.

text.p: The Swiss national airline Swissair seems headed for good returns in the first six months of this year, its chief operating officer said.
"It looks like the first half will be a good result for us," Jeffrey Katz told reporters at a briefing Monday. He gave no details.
In May, chairman Hannes Goetz of the parent group SAir Group, said it expected a markedly improved operating result in 1997.
In 1996, the group had an operating profit of 344 million Swiss francs ($235.1 million) but extraordinary charges of 739 million francs produced a net loss of 497 million.
Katz, a former vice-president of American Airlines who joined Swissair this year, said the company would be aiming to keep the lid on costs.
"Our challenge is the cost challenge....No airline can be successful without competitive cost," he said.
Swissair, would be aiming to grow but keep its current employee base, although some staff would not be replaced upon retirement.
Airlines had to have competitive cost, a good sales network and alliances with other carriers. "The world's too big to survive without alliances," said Katz.
Swissair aimed to strengthen its current alliances - with Belgium's Sabena, Austrian Airlines, Singapore Airlines and the U.S. Delta Air Lines.
The three European companies form with Delta the Atlantic Excellence partnership which recently announced an increase in the number of connections offered over the North Atlantic.
Katz said the link with Delta was unlikely to be changed in the near future despite reports of discussions between the U.S. company and French national carrier Air France AIRF.PA.
"Changing an alliance is a very complicated process. Our alliance with Delta is very well developed.
"They are going to have a tendency, as we are, to make it work," he added.
He confirmed that Swissair was looking for other Asian partners to expand the network offered by its alliance with Singapore Airlines.
"If you look at the wide geography of Asia and its huge population density, no one airline can cover it all," he said.
Swissair had made a number of contacts with other airlines in the region. "But none have advanced very far yet," he added.
